title: Edge-on Spiral Galaxy NGC 3628
caption: The edge-on spiral galaxy NGC 3628, imaged by the Mayall 4-meter Telescope
credit: T.A. Rector (University of Alaska Anchorage) and H. Schweiker (WIYN and NOIRLab/NSF/AURA)

recognition.text: Published in the NSF NOIRLab image archive. No published rating.

story: A large spiral galaxy seen edge-on stretches across this image, and a faint blue line reaches from it towards the upper-left corner. The galaxy is NGC 3628 in Leo, one of three galaxies known together as the Leo Triplet.
NGC 3628 is not quite the flat disc a spiral usually is. Its disc is warped, and that long, faint blue line is a tidal tail, a stream of stars and gas drawn out of the galaxy.

Both features are the result of gravity. Over time, the pull of the other two galaxies in the triplet has bent the disc and tugged material out into the tail. Galaxies that pass close to one another can reshape each other in this way, even without colliding directly, and faint tails like this one are often the clearest evidence of such encounters.

understand.summary: The Mosaic camera on the Mayall 4-meter Telescope used four filters. B is shown in blue, V in green, I in orange and hydrogen-alpha in red.
